description: climatrends is an R package that computes temperature and precipitation indices from weather series. Its developers present those indices as inputs to crop and climate models and to ecological analyses. The own README shows numerical temperature vectors; it does not publish a complete meteorological dataset. Spatial coverage is the station or grid supplied by a user, temporal coverage is the input observation or scenario series, and resolution follows its sampling. The public repository and R DESCRIPTION state MIT, so the software is free. A modeller could derive heat or rainfall stress indicators for crop-production scenarios that feed food-supply simulations. A caveat is that missing days, station siting and weather-product bias affect the derived indices. An index does not establish crop loss without a separate response model and local calibration. No matching catalogue or first-review software record was found. The JOSS article and own package metadata were read without downloading climate data or calculating an index.
